Asthma ED visits adults, age-adjusted rate per 10,000

prediction_scored: miss on the mechanism, unsettled on the test. I predicted a strong unadjusted association (1.3-3 per 10 ppb) carried by poverty, which would shrink by more than half on adjustment. The unadjusted estimate is 1.32 (0.65-2.65), imprecise, and adjustment moved it only to 1.22 (0.81-1.85), because NO2 and poverty are almost uncorrelated across UHF neighbourhoods (r = 0.05). Poverty alone gives 1.91 (1.62-2.25) per 10 percentage points and explains 50% of the variance in log rates; NO2 alone explains 2%.
settle: A neighbourhood cross-section with 42 units cannot detect an effect of the size the research reports (about 1.26 per 10 ppb), because poverty-linked variation in asthma ED use is far larger. A within-neighbourhood design would settle it: daily or weekly asthma ED counts by UHF (SPARCS or DOHMH syndromic surveillance) against daily NYCCAS or AQS concentrations, in a case-crossover or time-series model, so that each neighbourhood is its own control. A cohort with address-level NO2 (as in the NYC birth cohort studies) would test the long-term link.

notes: With borough fixed effects the NO2 ratio is 0.94 (0.51-1.74). PM2.5 adjusted for poverty: 1.04 (0.86-1.25) per 1 ug/m3 (research, Khreis 2017: 1.03 per 1 ug/m3). For adults (age-adjusted ED rate) the NO2 ratio adjusted for poverty is 0.86 (0.60-1.24). NO2 and PM2.5 are correlated at r = 0.95 across UHFs, so the two-pollutant model cannot separate them. The highest NO2 and PM2.5 are in midtown and lower Manhattan (UHF 306-310), where child asthma ED rates are low; the highest rates are in the South Bronx and East and Central Harlem (UHF 105-107, 302-303), where pollution is middling and poverty is high. The research slope drawn through the city mean is almost the same as the NYC unadjusted fit; the city data are consistent with the research but cannot confirm it. The EHDP 'asthma ED visits due to PM2.5' indicator was not used because it is computed from research concentration-response functions.
